*Generated by `ci/surface_audit.py`. Re-run with `make surface-audit`.*

never as a percentage — the denominator is `cdfc.surface.labels.SURFACES`, which is **append-only**
(see below).

Audited artifact: `reports/surface-audit/report.html`, 10,049 bytes, **zero external
references**.

| gate | | | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SG1** | ran | **PASS** | no banned token in the rendered text or in a reader-facing attribute |
| **SG2** | ran | **PASS** | render_ffr refuses all three uninformative cases and admits the fourth; no FFR appears on this surface yet (P14-B4 owns it) |

## What is NOT RUN, and it is the headline

`plan/07` specifies **SG1's DOM arm** (`page.inner_text` after JS) and **all of SG4**
(`getComputedStyle`, including `::before`/`::after` `content`) against a **headless browser**.
There is no headless browser in `requirements.lock` and no `pip` in this environment.

What ran instead is a **structural** arm: the artifact is parsed with `lxml` and the generated
stylesheet is read as data. Every assertion is about the bytes that ship, which is strictly weaker
than a computed style:

| the browser arm would catch | the structural arm |
|---|---|
| a `::before` pseudo-element injecting a glyph through `content:` | **misses it — the largest remaining hole in SG1** |
| a user-agent or cascade default the stylesheet does not state | misses it |
| a colour produced by blending, `filter`, or an unevaluated gradient | misses it |
| text inserted by JavaScript after load | **not applicable — this report ships no JavaScript at all**, so that half is closed by construction rather than by testing |

**A gate that cannot run is recorded as not run, never as passed.** Closing the gap needs a
headless browser in the lockfile; until then the structural arm is what the two integers above are
computed from, and this table is what qualifies them.

## The surface registry — APPEND-ONLY, because this phase's gate divides by it

The exit gate reads `surfaces_passing_all_four_gates == len(SURFACES)`, and **this build writes
`SURFACES`**. A surface that cannot be made to pass could be deleted and the gate would go green.
**That is M1 — the numerator choosing its own denominator — inside the gate meant to prevent it.**

So a row may be **retired** with a dated argument and **never deleted**; a retired row leaves the
gate's *denominator* and stays in the *scan*, because giving up on auditing a surface is not giving
up on prohibiting an affirmative claim on it.

| surface | kind | renders | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S01.report-file` | HTML | NONE | live |
| `S02.report-hero` | HTML | SETTLED_COUNT, STATE | live |
| `S03.report-strapline` | HTML | RATE, SETTLED_COUNT | live |
| `S04.report-band` | HTML | SETTLED_COUNT | live |
| `S05.report-openitems` | HTML | NONE | live |
| `S06.cli-version` | STDOUT | NONE | live |

**Cardinality: `|SURFACES|` = 6, live = 6, retired = 0.**
`tests/surface/test_surface_registry.py` asserts the registry has never shrunk, by diffing it against
`docs/SURFACE-REGISTRY-LOG.md` rather than against a previous commit — so the check survives a
squash.

## Two deviations from `plan/07`, recorded rather than left to be noticed

**1. The registry test is `tests/surface/test_surface_registry.py`, not `test_registry.py`.**
`plan/07` names the latter in four places. It cannot be used: `tests/unit/test_registry.py` already
exists, the test tree has no `__init__.py` files, and pytest therefore derives module names from
the basename — so the two collide and **collection aborts for the whole suite**.

The way it was found is the part worth keeping. **The negative-control sweep passed at 131/131
while this was broken**, because the sweep runs each entry's guards by node id in its own
subprocess and two files never get collected together. Only `make verify`'s full `pytest tests`
hits it. *A per-item harness cannot see a collision between items*, and that is a general property
of this sweep rather than a fact about this file.

**2. There are no `.j2` templates and no Jinja2.** See `src/cdfc/surface/markup.py` for the
argument; the short form is that Jinja's escaping is a constructor argument, and a flag is what
somebody sets when the deadline is Friday.

## P14-B2 — the Unchecked panel, and an OPEN finding that is not B2's

**B2 is complete and its own controls are green:** 136/136 catalogue entries caught, 221/221 guards
flipped, `contaminated_count 0`, every gate observed red including the three new ones.

**`make verify` nevertheless exits 2**, on
`tests/negative/test_nc_ingest.py::test_nc__P01_the_matrix_can_report_a_structural_disagreement`,
with `ResourceWarning: unclosed file <…FME…xlsx>` surfacing as a
`PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning` under this repo's `filterwarnings = ["error"]`.

**It is not B2's, and here is the evidence rather than the assertion:**

| | |
|---|---|
| the traceback's line | `reader_lxml.py:244`, which is **where the garbage collector happened to be running**, not where the file was opened |
| the class | **already documented in this repo.** `reader_openpyxl.py` carries a comment recording this exact shape: *"the garbage collector raises a ResourceWarning at whatever line happens to be executing when the finaliser runs — which fails an unrelated test and points the reader at innocent code. Found at P4 when a new dependency shifted collection order; it had been leaking a handle per read since P1"* |
| the two known leak sites | **both already fixed** — `container_guard.py` closes through `with zf:`, `reader_openpyxl.py` through `with closing(wb), closing(wbv)` |
| what B2 changed | nothing under `src/cdfc/ingest/`. It added tests, which changed **when** the collector runs |
| reproduction | **does not reproduce** running `tests/negative` alone, nor either affected test in isolation |

**So there is at least one leaked handle still unlocated**, it is pre-existing, and it surfaces at a
line that has nothing to do with it. Locating it needs `PYTHONTRACEMALLOC`, which slows the suite
past the point of usefulness in this environment.

**FOUND AND FIXED, 16 Aug 2026.** `qualify/template_instrument.py::_party_b` loaded a workbook and
never closed it — the one opener under `src/` with neither a context manager nor a `close()`. It is
the **second** reader to do this (`reader_openpyxl.py` was the first, at P4), so the repair is a
**structural guard** rather than one more fix:
`tests/contract/test_contract__handles_are_closed.py` walks every `.py` under `src/cdfc/` by AST
and asserts that every `load_workbook` and `ZipFile` result is closed — through a `with`, through
`contextlib.closing`, or through an explicit `.close()`. It was observed red against the very
defect it was written for, and it carries an admission-side control asserting the walk actually
reaches the three known openers, because a walk that matched nothing would pass while checking
nothing.

**How it was located.** A throwaway pytest plugin collecting garbage after every test — the
finaliser then runs at a known point instead of wherever the collector happens to be. That run
passed cleanly, which was itself the finding: *prompt collection prevents the cross-test
contamination*, so the leak was real and its damage was entirely in **when** it surfaced. The
remaining work was a direct search for openers, which found one.

`make verify` after the fix: **136/136 entries caught, 221/221 guards flipped,
`contaminated_count 0`, 115 of 115 live gates observed red, 0 PENDING, exit 0.**

*The paragraph below is retained as written at the time, because the reasoning it records is why
the fix took the shape it did.*

**This was recorded as OPEN rather than worked around.** The tempting fix — a `gc.collect()` in a
conftest fixture — would make the warning surface at its own module and would also make it *stop
failing the build*, which is the wrong direction: the warning is true, a handle is leaking, and the
build going red about it is the system working. What is wrong is only that it accuses the wrong
line.
